basis: Skeletal dysplasia, diabetes and deafness define disease; dentin defects occur in 4/4. Mild intellectual disability (4/4) omitted at cap; diabetic retinopathy is separate.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dentinogenesis imperfecta in 4/4 and tooth loss in 2/4; retained as the fourth axis under the primary cap.
decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural hearing loss is a named defining feature, present in 4/4.

basis: Central respiratory/autonomic failure defines disease; achalasia and intestinal dysmotility occur in 3/3; scoliosis and kyphosis each occur in 1/3.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: persistent hypoventilation and apnea define the syndrome's loss of ventilatory function, despite its central origin.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural spinal deformity is documented as scoliosis and kyphosis, each in 1/3, meeting the supplied 30% threshold.

basis: Hormone excess defines the syndrome. Diarrhea and flushing do not establish tissue damage; underlying tumors are separate. Cardiac lesions are annotated at 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: frequent secretory diarrhea does not establish intestinal tissue damage; intestinal carcinoid tumors are separately diagnosed.

basis: Developmental disability and ocular malformations define disease; respiratory failure is annotated at 80-99%. Thin skin and sparse hair lack documented functional impairment.

decisions.dermatologic: none: thin skin and sparse hair occur in 4/4, but these descriptive anomalies do not establish skin damage or functional loss.

basis: Subcutaneous, oral/visceral and upper-airway edema are defining disease sites. Bradykinin-mediated RAAS-blocker angioedema is not inherently immune-mediated.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: upper-airway edema is explicitly a defining disease location; the 5-29% obstruction frequency does not exclude a primary site.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral tissues and viscera are disease sites; tongue and lip edema are annotated at 30-79%. Transience does not exclude the disease's primary location.

basis: Central and peripheral neurologic dysfunction defines disease; hypodontia occurs in 80-99%. Distal amyotrophy reflects denervation rather than established intrinsic muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy at 30-79% reflects neurogenic muscle wasting; direct skeletal muscle disease is not established.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining early neurodegeneration: regression in 5/5 and cerebellar atrophy in 3/5. Visual loss occurs in 2/5 (40%); optic atrophy is documented.

decisions.neurologic: primary: early neurodevelopmental regression and encephalopathy define the clinical syndrome; regression occurs in 5/5 and seizures in 4/5.

basis: Mosaic Down syndrome is a neurodevelopmental disorder; congenital heart defects occur in approximately 40% of mosaic cases, supporting direct cardiovascular involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital heart defects affect approximately 40% of mosaic Down syndrome cases, exceeding the 30% threshold.

basis: Growth restriction, skeletal asymmetry and digital abnormalities define SRS1. Hypoglycemia occurs in roughly 25-30%; consistent endocrine gland disease is not established.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: syndromic growth restriction alone is not endocrine disease; hypoglycemia occurs in roughly 25-30% and is not a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Lipodystrophy/insulin resistance, Rieger anomaly and skeletal features define SHORT; hearing loss is annotated at 80-99%. Dental and skin/subcutis abnormalities omitted at cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none under cap: dental delay occurs in 6/6 and enamel defects in 30-79%; retained axes capture greater functional burden.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal growth abnormalities, delayed bone maturation and joint hypermobility are defining features; hypermobility occurs in 80-99%.
